None of the exclusion clauses apply here, and PLP as a gene is a causal agent, so despite representing a spectrum of disorders rather than one entity, I'll lean toward classifying "PLP-associated disease" as Specific Disease under the individuating-anchor rule.

For "the disease is progressive rather than static in some," that's bare anaphoric reference to the disease already mentioned, so it falls under the "not labeled" category.

Going through the rest: "signs of disease" stays bare and unlabeled, while "mental retardation is not severe" fits the grey-area Disease Class treatment from the earlier example. For "dementia or personality disorders," I'm weighing whether this is two separate Disease Class labels versus a Composite Mention since they're coordinated disease names sharing an elided head—I'll go with Composite Mention since the coordination rule applies regardless of syntactic slot.

For "nystagmus is absent" and "tremors are prominent," I'm checking whether these sign nouns pass the pathological-state frame test since they appear in a characterizing "differs...in that" clause about the disease form—I'll annotate both as Disease Class since they function as arguments of a characterizing predicate, alongside "mental retardation," even though this risks over-annotation.
